business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Aseptic Barista-Formula Hydrolyzed Oat Milk

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU (Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union) – Germany Double Taxation Agreement (2012, as amended)
BLEU – France Double Taxation Agreement (1958, as amended by the 2006 Protocol)
BLEU – Netherlands Double Taxation Convention (1970, as amended by the 2015 Protocol)
Luxembourg – Hong Kong Double Taxation Agreement (2010)
Luxembourg – United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (1967, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (AML/CFT Law, as amended, including by the Law of 13 January 2019); Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016 introducing Article 25-1 (SCSp); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); implementing Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 January 2019; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF AML/CFT Guidelines (latest consolidated version 2024); Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector (where a regulated general partner is appointed).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of the foreign corporate partner's constitutional documents (statutes/charter) with French or German sworn translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign trade register or competent corporate registry of the partner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Convention of 5 October 1961 where applicable; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing (extrait du registre) of each foreign corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry (e.g., Companies House, Handelsregister, RCS)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney granted to the Luxembourg incorporation counsel and domiciliation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin, apostilled as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid passport copies, proof of residential address and source-of-funds evidence for each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) of the partner entities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent public authority issuing the passport, complemented by utility/rent certificate and bank statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copies with sworn French/German translation; apostille of the notarial certificate

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence (CDD) under Articles 3 and 4 of the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004. Screening of all UBOs, general partners and authorized signatories against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (including Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and Regulation (EC) 2580/2001), the UN Security Council consolidated list, the OFAC SDN list for USD-denominated transactions, and Luxembourg national restrictive measures. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) mandatory for politically exposed persons (PEPs) pursuant to FATF Recommendations 12 and 22. Suspicious transactions must be reported without undue delay to the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) online portal via www.lbr.lu and the eJustice platform of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg (justice.public.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be expressed in Latin script; French and German are accepted procedural languages for RCS filings. Accented Latin characters and Luxembourgish toponyms are permitted; names derived from non-Latin alphabets must be transliterated into Latin script with a sworn translation. The SCSp name must be preceded or followed by the compulsory suffix 'SCSp' or the full expression 'société en commandite spéciale'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg / national / état / commune (sovereign and public-law terms requiring Grand-Ducal or ministerial authorization)
banque / bank / crédit / trust (regulated banking and financial terms requiring a CSSF license)
assurance / insurance / réassurance (regulated insurance terms requiring approval by the Commissariat aux Assurances)
fonds / UCITS / SICAV / SIF / RAIF / ARIF (regulated fund terminology requiring CSSF prior authorization)
université / lycée / école (educational titles requiring Ministry of Education consent)
notaire / avocat / réviseur d'entreprises / expert-comptable (reserved professional titles requiring the consent of the relevant professional body)
wine / crémant / champagne (protected geographical indications requiring agricultural authority clearance)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant may, within 15 days of the rejection notification, submit a written reconsideration request to the LBR registration department. If the rejection is maintained, an appeal lies to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Commercial Chamber) under the procedures applicable to the Law of 10 August 1915; the appeal must be filed within two (2) months of the final administrative refusal. Alternatively, the applicant may re-run the LBR name availability search and file a new name reservation within the same day.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for an industrial UHT plant manufacturing operation. Article 25-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915 requires the SCSp to maintain its registered office (siège social) in Luxembourg. Licensed corporate domiciliation is accepted for holding or administrative functions, but is not sufficient commercial substance for ISIC 1050 manufacturing; physical production premises, operational infrastructure, and locally based operational management are required to obtain the commercial establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011 and to register as a food business operator with the Luxembourg Veterinary and Food Administration (ALVA) under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 35% annual likelihood of unannounced physical inspection once the plant is operational, driven primarily by ALVA food-safety inspections coordinated with the Ministry of Health, and by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT/TVA audits. Pre-incorporation phase: approximately 5% likelihood of an on-site inspection by the Ministry of the Economy in connection with the commercial establishment permit.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official company name availability check and RCS name clearance certificate (certificat de non-confusion)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 21 December 2013 on RCS fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS electronic incorporation filing for the SCSp (online lodging of the partnership agreement and supporting documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: LBR electronic filing statutory tariff (EUR 19 base fee plus per-partner annex fees)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legalization and notarization bundle for foreign partner documents (apostilles, sworn French/German translations, notarial certificates for two corporate partners)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Origin-country notaries, apostille authorities and Luxembourg sworn translators
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 450–650 per partner entity set; varies by origin jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO (RBE) initial registration filing under the Law of 13 January 2019 submitted by incorporation counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RBE register; statutory filing is free of charge, amount reflects counsel compliance fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Service fee benchmark (registration itself free under Article 11 of the Law of 13 January 2019)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory electronic publication tariff per page after RCS registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation agreement – first 12 months (licensed corporate domiciliation service)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation company (agréé by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 200–280 per month for licensed domiciliation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) and compilation of the pre-incorporation KYC/AML file – external counsel fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional market benchmark EUR 5,500–8,000 fixed fee for a two-partner SCSp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial PEP / OFAC / UN / EU sanctions database screening of all UBOs and partners and formal AML compliance memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm / AML compliance software provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 350–450 per screening cycle, subject to volume and database access

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 903-907 (Société en Commandite Spéciale); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register, Articles 8-12; Law of 10 June 1999 on Classified Establishments, Articles 1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 6, avenue du Swing, L-4367 Belvaux; online filing through lbr.lu / eregistration.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for registration (demande d'immatriculation au RCS) with the statutory declaration of conformity (déclaration de conformité), the executed partnership agreement (contrat de société), and the registered-office consent.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital or escrow account is imposed on an SCSp under Articles 903-907 of the 1915 Companies Act. Contributions are freely fixed in the partnership agreement; the banking benchmark for the target plant is at least EUR 50,000 paid-in cash contribution, plus in-kind capital items (leasehold improvements, processing equipment licences) described in a contribution schedule appended to the agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Unanimous Resolutions of the Founding Partners of the SCSp governed by Article 903 et seq. of the amended Law of 10 August 1915: (1) the capital contributions and profit-sharing ratios of the limited partners as set out in the partnership agreement are ratified and recorded; (2) the registered office of the firm is established at [address, Luxembourg], Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg; (3) [Name] is appointed general partner (associé commandité) and managing representative, with authority to open and operate bank accounts, execute trade contracts, file statutory applications, and bind the firm in the construction, licensing, and equipping of its UHT oat-milk packaging plant; (4) the resolution is effective immediately and may be relied upon by the RCS, banks, and public authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-formation drafting, name availability screening, and partner AML/KYC due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS name database) through an authorised Luxembourg domiciliation and formation agency or law firm.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) with the management clause of the general partner, free or restricted transferability of the limited partner interests, registered office clause and contribution schedule. Screen the proposed corporate name against the RCS database. Collect statutory due-diligence documents, including criminal record certificates and source-of-funds statements, and obtain a written consent of the registered-office provider.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement with SCSp-specific provisions under Articles 903-907
RCS name availability extract
Valid passport or national ID and proof of residential address for each founding partner
Certificate of good conduct (extrait du casier judiciaire) for the natural-person general partner
AML/KYC questionnaires, source-of-funds statement and beneficial-owner organigram
Domiciliation agreement and address consent of the Luxembourg registered-office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the corporate name or a contractual clause, the formation agent amends the draft and re-submits electronically within five business days; for enhanced AML/KYC queries, additional bank references and source-of-wealth exhibits are supplied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership agreement, adoption of the first resolution and contribution deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding parties assisted by a Luxembourg notary (optional) or acting under LuxTrust electronic signature; contribution escrow held with a Luxembourg payment institution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the constitutive meeting of the partners, adopt the pro-forma first resolution, and execute the partnership agreement. Open a temporary contribution account for the firm's name, deposit the cash contribution, and obtain a bank attestation of funds. For any in-kind contribution, record the item, valuation and transfer warranty in a schedule to the agreement.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (original wet-ink or LuxTrust e-signed PDF)
Pro-forma first board/general-partner resolution minutes
Bank attestation of deposit of the cash contribution
Signature specimen of the general partner and managing representative
AML file with the source-of-funds trail for the contributed capital
Schedule of in-kind contributions, if any, with agreed valuations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the bank refuses the contribution attestation for residual KYC reasons, the general partner substitutes a sworn statement of contribution irrevocability and completes the constitution of contributions within 30 days after RCS registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, e-Registration portal (eregistration.lu).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the electronic registration application signed by the general partner or the authorized agent using LuxTrust; attach the executed partnership agreement, the declaration of conformity, certified identity documents, and registered-office consent; pay the statutory fee online; retain the automatic filing acknowledgement and RCS file number.
required_dossiers: Application for RCS registration (demande d'immatriculation)
Statutory declaration of conformity (déclaration de conformité) signed by the general partner
Certified copy of the executed partnership agreement
Certified copies of identity documents of partners and beneficial owners
Registered-office consent / domiciliation certificate
Proof of payment of the RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a deficiency notice (avis de carence), the agent submits the missing instrument within the granted time limit (usually 15 days); materially incorrect filings can be corrected through the rectification procedure without re-paying the registration fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA publication and activation of VAT, EORI and social security identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RESA), Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), and Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the LBR automatically publishes the registration extract in the electronic compendium (RESA). File the VAT registration form and EORI application through the guichet.lu business portal; register the managing representative for social security with the CCSS and request the accident-insurance registration from the Association d'assurance accident (AAA).
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract issued after the filing
Executed partnership agreement and appointment proof of the managing partner
RCS extract indicating the physical operating address of the UHT plant
VAT (form 010) and EORI registration applications
NACE/ISIC business activity declaration (10.51 or 10.89 to be confirmed for oat-milk processing)
Bank reference data for social security direct-debit obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT delays issuance of the VAT number beyond the service standard, the tax counsel files a formal reminder with the case reference and may request priority handling; the SCSp is treated as a taxable person for VAT purposes and shall not issue VAT invoices before the number is granted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Classified establishment pre-application and environmental screening for the UHT plant
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'environnement in co-ordination with the Ministry of the Economy, Direction générale de l'Industrie.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the pre-application dossier (avant-projet) for the establishment of the aseptic UHT oat-milk packaging plant as a classified installation under the amended Law of 10 June 1999. Provide site layout, loading and discharge points, installed boiler capacity, CIP/ammonia refrigeration inventories, and requested class tier. Request the environmental impact screening decision within the statutory phase before any works are commissioned.
required_dossiers: Architectural/site plan with structural load certificate for the process hall
Preliminary environmental screening form and hazard identification annex
Water abstraction and wastewater discharge projections of the UHT and CIP modules
Ammonia and F-gas refrigeration inventory with safety datasheets
Steam boiler specifications, fuel type and stack emission calculations
Waste management plan for packaging, finished-product losses and CIP effluents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Administration requires the full environmental impact assessment, the applicant proceeds with the scoping report and public inquiry within the statutory window; any classification decision can be challenged before the administrative tribunal within three months of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy, Direction générale de l'Industrie et de l'Énergie; Administration de la Sécurité Alimentaire (Food Safety Administration) under the Ministry of Health; Administration de l'environnement for the classified-establishment permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Classified Establishment Operating Authorisation (autorisation d'exploiter un établissement classé) under the amended Law of 10 June 1999; Food Business Operator Registration and Approval for the UHT oat-milk aseptic packaging facility under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement, Département de l'Environnement, Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 2 classified establishment ('autorisation d'exploiter') with an environmental impact screening; a full EIA report is triggered only where the daily raw-input capacity of oat-based liquid reaches 200 tonnes/day (EIA Directive 2011/92/EU Annex II threshold for milk processing, applied by analogy) or where aggregate steam boiler capacity reaches 50 MWth or more.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater pre-treated to sewer: pH 6.5-9.5, BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, COD ≤ 1,000 mg/L, TSS ≤ 600 mg/L, total N ≤ 60 mg/L, total P ≤ 10 mg/L; direct surface-water discharge after biological treatment: BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L, total N ≤ 10 mg/L, total P ≤ 1 mg/L; gas-fired medium combustion boilers (Directive (EU) 2015/2193): NOx ≤ 200 mg/Nm³ and CO ≤ 100 mg/Nm³; solvent VOC concentration ≤ 75 mg/Nm³; ammonia refrigeration compliance with Regulation (EU) 517/2014; packaging waste quota compliance with Directive 94/62/EC.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification through the communal fire-prevention commission and Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours covering escape routes, sprinkler cover and the ammonia machine room; structural load inspection approval for the aseptic hall and high-bay packaging warehouse; workplace clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines for CIP chemicals (NaOH/H2O2), noise exposure, thermal hazards and pressure equipment, plus registration with the Association d'assurance accident for industrial accident cover.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; central e-services and filings via MyGuichet.lu; official portals impotsdirects.public.lu and pfi.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Appoint a Luxembourg general partner or service provider and obtain a Luxembourg registered office for the SCSp; obtain the sectoral business licence (autorisation d'établissement) and food-safety approval required for UHT oat-milk manufacturing. 2) File the SCSp instrument and UBO details electronically with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), obtaining the RCS registration number. 3) Apply to the AEDT for VAT identification through MyGuichet using the VAT identification request form, stating turnover and activity; if the SCSp is non-established, also appoint an approved tax representative (responsable solidaire). 4) Apply to the ACD for the direct-tax file or matricule number where direct tax filings are required; for a transparent SCSp the partners report their share on their own Luxembourg or foreign returns. 5) Register as an employer with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) if staff are hired.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - the Luxembourg SCSp is fiscally transparent for direct tax purposes; profits are taxed at partner level and the partnership itself is not subject to corporate income tax, although it may be subject to municipal business tax to the extent it exercises a commercial activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no US-style check-the-box election. The transparent classification of the SCSp is the statutory default. In a hybrid situation, when another jurisdiction treats the SCSp as opaque, Luxembourg will apply ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules and the parties must document the divergence, report any resulting deduction or non-inclusion mismatch, and align the transaction with the substance requirements; no separate voluntary entity-classification form is available for income tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA - taxe sur la valeur ajoutée), implemented in accordance with the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established micro and small businesses, excluding one-off exempt supplies; non-established foreign suppliers are not covered by the exemption threshold and must register for Luxembourg VAT from their first taxable supply in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control mandate is currently imposed on B2B invoices in Luxembourg. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory for public-sector suppliers through the PEPPOL network. Structured e-invoices such as UBL, CII and EDIFACT are accepted for audit; Luxembourg will transpose the EU VAT-in-the-Digital-Age e-invoicing and digital reporting requirements once the EU framework is adopted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rating applies when UHT oat-milk products are physically transported from Luxembourg out of the EU to a non-EU customer, title and risk pass to that customer, and the exporter holds credible transport and customs evidence. Services: B2B international services are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT when the place of supply is outside the EU; zero-rating may apply to services directly connected with export transport and ancillary services. The supply is not zero-rated when goods are placed on the Luxembourg domestic market or dispatched to another EU Member State.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (single administrative document or SAD) with export customs office validation
Bill of lading, CMR consignment note or air waybill proving physical departure from the EU
Export contract, purchase order or letter of credit
Inward remittance certificate or bank SWIFT MT103 / TT wire confirmation evidencing foreign exchange settlement
Delivery and acceptance proof from the non-EU customer or warehouse records
EC sales list and Intrastat declarations where an EU intra-Community dispatch is separately exempted
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is scrutinised through documentary audits; if satisfactory contemporaneous evidence is not produced, the Luxembourg VAT authority reassesses the supply at 17%, charges default interest from the due date, applies administrative fines of up to 100% of the underpaid VAT, and may seek clawback of refunds. Criminal tax-fraud proceedings can lead to fines up to double the evaded tax and imprisonment. The ordinary limitation period is five years, extended to ten years in cases of intentional fraud or serious tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem framework, alongside the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance for foreign exchange and balance-of-payments oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a participating Member State of the European Monetary Union; the euro is fully convertible. There is no exchange control law, no capital transfer authorization regime, and no restriction on current or capital account movements under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). Profit and capital remittances are not subject to FX control hurdles. The SCSp, being a transparent partnership for Luxembourg tax purposes, benefits from the same unrestricted capital movement principles; however, any bank transaction is subject to normal EU AML reporting, CSSF supervision, and counterparty compliance screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender obligations, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no legal requirement to repatriate or liquidate export receipts in Luxembourg or any other Eurozone jurisdiction. Proceeds may be retained in any currency in a euro-denominated or multicurrency account, subject only to standard banking documentation and AML/CFT record-keeping under the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004, as amended, and EU Regulation 2015/847.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency transaction and payroll), Capital Escrow Account for third-party investor contribution ring-fencing
Operational Account (EUR and USD), Capital Escrow Account, trade finance and documentary credit account
Operational Account (EUR, GBP, USD), Capital Escrow Account, short-term money market and FX hedging facility
Operational Account and Commercial LC settlement account; Capital Escrow Account where required by co-investor side letters
Operational Account, dedicated commodity-trade accounts, Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for non-EEA offshore digital EMI providers and High-Medium for EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) exercising a valid passport into Luxembourg under the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2, Directive (EU) 2015/2366). An offshore EMI without an EEA passport cannot lawfully hold client funds or provide payment accounts for the SCSp. Even with a valid passport, an EMI may only issue e-money and provide payment services; it may not operate as a full commercial bank for purposes of taking deposits, holding capital under an escrow with bank-guarantee features, or granting overdraft/trade credit. The principal legal constraint is the CSSF’s requirement that all payment services providers conduct their own, non-delegable AML/KYC assessment of the SCSp, its general partner, the registered office, and all beneficial owners. The EMI is therefore viable only as a supplementary settlement rail, not as the primary treasury bank for UHT plant construction and trade disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Luxembourg statute unconditionally mandates a physical board meeting at the bank’s premises, but CSSF-compliant bank practice for a non-resident SCSp with non-resident partners generally requires either (a) a physical one-on-one meeting with at least one authorized signatory and the ultimate beneficial owner (or a professional director holding a valid power of attorney), or (b) a remote video-identification session supplemented by a Luxembourg notary or a qualified 'professional of the financial sector' attestation as permitted under CSSF AML/CFT circulars. In practice, tier-one banks classify the SCSp as an international corporate under enhanced scrutiny, and a physical or hybrid interview with the general partner and UBO is recommended for High viability onboarding. If the SCSp is represented by a Luxembourg-regulated fiduciary or management company, that professional can perform the interview mandate under a documented reliance framework.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Indirect or non-transparent ownership through a Special LP (SCSp) with non-resident limited partners and no minimum capital requirement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the notarized or private deed of the SCSp; excerpt of the Luxembourg Register of Commerce (RCS) showing the general partner and registered office; up-to-date register of limited partners (if maintained and not statutorily confidential) or a sworn declaration from the general partner identifying all beneficial owners; organizational chart issued by a Luxembourg law firm; detailed source-of-wealth narrative for each limited partner; relevant consent letters from the CSSF or the FIU where a non-standard opacity flag is raised.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk or offshore residency of one or more limited partners controlling more than 25% of the SCSp capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passports, proof of residential address, tax residence certificates for each relevant partner; sworn statement of source of funds and source of wealth; corporate documentary evidence for institutional investors, including constitutional documents, board resolutions authorizing the investment, and audited financial statements; sanctions and PEP screening results processed through a licensed compliance provider; evidence that no politically exposed person is involved unless proper PEP acceptance procedures are applied.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution originating from a third country in a non-EUR currency without transparent FX purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed capital contribution agreement or subscription agreement; bank reference letter from the remitting institution; proof of the underlying industrial project (E.g. UHT oat milk plant construction contract, ISIC 1050 manufacturing license application); invoice or SPA for the plant equipment; a sworn treasury statement explaining the currency conversion requirements; IBAN/SWIFT cover details showing a clear remittance chain; written confirmation that funds will be used for capital expenditure and operational disbursements only.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of statutory business license or operating permit for the UHT aseptic oat milk plant at the time of onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the submitted application for the Luxembourg or jurisdiction-specific food manufacturing license; ISIC 1050 / NAICS 311999 classification certificate; Ministry of Health or food safety agency preliminary approval letter; engineering and architectural plan for the UHT plant; evidence of compliance with the Pasteurized Milk Ordinance and aseptic packaging standards; third-party certification roadmap from SGS, Bureau Veritas, or equivalent; projected commissioning timeline and permit-to-operation schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Anticipated high transaction velocity and third-party disbursements to suppliers in multiple jurisdictions for plant machinery, packaging materials, and oat concentrate.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed 12-month treasury forecast by counterparty and purpose; executed commercial contracts and pro-forma invoices; supply chain due diligence files; transfer-pricing documentation showing arm's-length payment terms; a fully executed intercompany loan or capital call agreement if funds will be advanced by partners; bank-mandated anti-money laundering transaction monitoring will be supported by a periodic compliance report prepared by the Luxembourg tax advisor and AML counsel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols require the general partner of the SCSp to issue a capital call notice and receive funds via SWIFT or TARGET2 into the designated operational account. There is no Luxembourg exchange control approval requirement, but each inbound transfer must be tagged with clear remittance information such as 'SCSp capital contribution – UHT plant project' or 'Limited partner loan under section 4 of the partnership agreement'. The bank will apply standard AML/KYC verification of the remitter, the underlying partnership deed, the RCS registration, and the source of funds. Purpose codes used by correspondent banks may be generated automatically from the beneficiary field; however, the SCSp must ensure that the remitter states the OECD or local category code for foreign direct investment in manufacturing (Type: direct investment, sector ISIC 1050) when required by the remitting jurisdiction, while Luxembourg itself imposes no reporting beyond the BCL statistical balance-of-payments declaration. For amounts exceeding EUR 10,000 or any cash equivalent, EU Regulation 2015/847 payment information requirements apply and must be embedded in the wire transfer message. Inbound USD or third-currency wires should be routed through a US or intermediary correspondent in accordance with OFAC sanctions screening; the receiving Luxembourg bank will use the MT103 or Fedwire cover payment instructions and will reconcile the final credit to the SCSp's EUR or multicurrency account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for outbound trade settlements is SWIFT MT103 / MT202 for direct wire transfers; for supplier payments in Europe, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer within the Single Euro Payments Area; for structural equipment and packing-line purchases, Commercial Letters of Credit governed by ICC Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600) and the eUCP. TARGET2 is the mandated euro settlement system for all large-value EUR transactions and ensures irrevocable final settlement. For commodity contracts involving oat concentrate and packaging film, the SCSp should use an irrevocable, confirming bank LC confirmed by the seller’s bank; the corresponding documents will be negotiated through SWIFT MT700, MT710, MT720, and MT754 messages. The bank may require a separate reimbursement account for LC maturities; outbound payments must be accompanied by invoices, delivery confirmations, and inspection certificates to meet KYC and anti-money-laundering transaction monitoring. The SCSp can also use the same bank’s trade finance front end to create electronic bank payment obligations (EBO) for supply-chain finance, provided the beneficiary bank accepts parametrized payment undertakings. Any outbound payment in a non-EUR currency will be processed through the FX spot desk; no Luxembourg approval is required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF up to twelve months tenor
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for exotic currencies such as BRL, ZAR, or INR, where liquidity constraints prevent physical delivery
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) for liquidity transformation between multicurrency income and USD capex obligations
Plain-vanilla currency options, including call/put combinations and collars, subject to board authorization and EMIR reporting
Inflation-indexed swaps denominated in EUR, insofar as linked to plant construction inflation exposure
Interest rate swaps, where necessary, to hedge term loan repricing but limited to liability-management hedging under the SCSp's treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration of continuity and updated registration details (RCS 'déclaration annuelle')
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: within one month following the RCS registration anniversary; for an SCSp registered on 10 March, the filing closes on 10 April of every year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal reminder from the RCS; continuing default triggers a coercive fine (astreinte) of EUR 50 per day up to EUR 5,000, and after court-ordered enforcement remains unheeded the RCS may initiate strike-off/dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (RBE confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same anniversary filing period as the RCS annual declaration; due within one month after each RCS registration anniversary and filed jointly through LBR's e-filing platform.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violations of the Beneficial Owner Act (Act of 13 January 2019) are criminally sanctionable; legal persons may be fined EUR 250,000 to EUR 1,250,000 and managers imprisoned up to five years. LBR may also refuse to issue excerpts/certificates until the confirmation is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (active only if SCSp exemption is unavailable — corporate general partner or large-undertaking status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts must be approved within six months of the financial year-end (31 December for calendar-year accounts) and filed within one month of approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit exposes the general partner to court-ordered astreinte up to EUR 5,000, criminal fines for responsible managers, and, if the default persists, RCS strike-off and judicial winding-up.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate for corporate partners in Luxembourg City (17% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax); SCSp itself is fiscally transparent and not a CIT taxpayer.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for SCSp; effective relief arises from transparency, 100% participation exemption for qualifying corporate partners, and the 80% IP box deduction (approximate 4.99% effective rate).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 750 / Formulaire 750 (corporate income tax return) filed via ACD e-CDF/MyGuichet.lu; the SCSp files an informational transparent-entity annex rather than a full CIT liability return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly CIT prepayments applied through partner declarations (installments due 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year (e.g. 30 June for a calendar-year SCSp); extension may be granted by the Administration des contributions directes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS number, Luxembourg tax number, status as Société en Commandite Spéciale.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert Luxembourg general partner details; non-resident limited partners are not locally taxable merely as partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial profit or loss per annual accounts before partner allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate taxable share to each partner according to the partnership agreement; file no SCSp-level tax on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of fines, excessive shareholder remuneration, and non-documented intra-group charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners add back only their allocated share of Luxembourg-source non-deductible expenditure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption, IP box, and other relieving provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty resident partners must provide a TRC and a principal-purpose-test-compliant statement before claiming exemption in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of intercompany UHT plant purchases, royalty flows, and contract manufacturing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach local-file summary if any related-party transaction exists; arm's-length result must be demonstrated.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an ex-officio assessment, a 10% surcharge if filed after formal warning, and monthly default interest of 0.6% on unpaid tax; intentional non-filing may be prosecuted as tax evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on SCSp profit distributions because the SCSp is pass-through; had the profit been paid as a dividend by an opaque Luxembourg company, the statutory rate would be 15%, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or an applicable DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For an SCSp, no Luxembourg withholding is imposed at distribution; non-resident partners therefore take the distribution as taxable in their country of residence. If treaty relief is triggered, the beneficial owner must obtain a certificate of tax residence (Formulaire 790 / ‘Certificat de résidence’) from the relevant tax authority and file the Luxembourg DTA relief application before the payment date, also confirming that the SCSp is not used as a conduit under the principal purpose test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to a non-resident creditor: 0% Luxembourg withholding tax. Royalties for trademarks, process know-how and technology licensing: 15% statutory withholding tax; usually reduced to 0% under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive for associated EU companies or under selected DTAs; non-EU treaty rates commonly provide 0% or 5%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File and CbCR threshold: EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group turnover. Local File: no separate statutory monetary threshold; the Luxembourg tax administration may request supporting TP documentation for any related-party transaction in an audit. Administrative expectation: a full local-file TP study should be in place when related-party cross-border turnover exceeds EUR 1,000,000 per annum.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but it applies OECD BEPS minimum standards, the ATAD anti-abuse rules, and Luxembourg GAAR. The SCSp must demonstrate real physical substance, local management, personnel, and economic purpose in Luxembourg to avoid reclassification as an abusive shell and to obtain treaty access.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting oat-milk manufacturing revenues, inflating intra-group UHT processing fees, or maintaining undisclosed foreign bank accounts for payments received under SWIFT LC / TT wire rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment by ACD plus default interest at 0.6% per month; criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment up to five years and fines up to EUR 250,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner of the SCSp has unlimited liability; directors who knowingly signed false declarations are jointly and severally liable for taxes, interest, and fines, and may face asset seizure and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Misuse / Lack of Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp maintains no physical office, no UHT plant personnel, no board/management meetings in Luxembourg, and no decision-making for the aseptic oat milk operation; it exists solely to route income through Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the SCSp under GAAR, denial of treaty benefits under the principal purpose test, reclassification of profit distributions as taxable dividends, and application of 24.94% aggregate CIT plus net wealth tax at partner level.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil and hold the general partner and de facto directors personally liable for reinstated tax liabilities, including concealed partnership debts and pecuniary penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to declare the ultimate beneficial owner in the Luxembourg RCS UBO register; accepting anonymous limited partners; executing wire transfers without customer due diligence or beneficial ownership identification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 for legal persons and criminal penalties including imprisonment for up to five years for natural persons; the regulator may block distributions and revoke the partnership's license if required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML compliance officers, directors and the managing general partner are personally liable for fines and civil confiscation of illicit profits; repeated violations result in disqualification from managing Luxembourg entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing or materially flawed TP local file on cross-border oat-milk supply and licensing; royalty rate set without functional analysis; no documentation of risks absorbed by the Luxembourg UHT plant.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg tax authorities may adjust profits to arm's-length, levy a 10% documentation penalty and monthly interest, and recharacterize excess royalty as a taxable deemed distribution subject to 15% withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner is personally liable for the restored corporation tax and dividend withholding tax; professional directors who approved false TP files face joint liability and disqualification.
